lines.text: They still have cognitive function, but their brainwaves are Patterned. We couldn't determine if they're conscious or not. And some are already dead, at least. What should we do?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37307
lines.text: Make them comfortable. Pain medication. That's all we can do.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37327
lines.text: Hey, any updates on our staffing request?

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63338
lines.text: Well, some members of the Resource Approval Committee are MIA, so the committee can't meet. And they can't replace anyone until the MIAs are confirmed dead.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37325
lines.text: The Resource Approval Committee?

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63336
lines.text: I was sent to talk to the staffing supervisor, but well, he won't budge without a ruling from the committee. So...  I've put in a request for a Director overrule, Acting Director overrule, but well, that'll take hours.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37323
lines.text: God...

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37322
lines.text: Hey, the FBC is issuing me a name plate and I have to pick a color: stormy gray or charcoal gray?

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63333
lines.text: Hmm... Charcoal gray?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37320
lines.text: Huh, what made you-- No I can't do it. They look exactly the same.

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63331
lines.text: Can I see them to compare?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37318
lines.text: What? No. I don't understand why they keep wasting my time with this stuff. I have patients.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37316
lines.text: Oh my god.

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63329
lines.text: I mean, you want a good nameplate. The contrast. Lettering. Sturdy. What materials are they offering this year?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37303
lines.text: How exactly does the FBC get funding? Do you know?

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63314
lines.text: Nope. I'm not in accounting.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37301
lines.text: You're not curious how your tax dollars are used? Or how a secret government agency gets money without public oversight?

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63312
lines.text: Not really.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37299
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63310
lines.text: 2.39672 and one three thirty--

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37297
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63308
lines.text: The numbers you asked for earlier.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37295
lines.text: Start again?

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63306
lines.text: 2.39672 and one three thirty eight. 3.15829 and two seven hundred. Should I keep going? You're not writing it down.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37293
lines.text: I have good memory.

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63304
lines.text: 6.78899 and twenty-five hundred. 1.00982 and sixteen. 9.28838 and eighty-five hundred. 5.67281 and sixty-three.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37291
lines.text: Good.

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63297
lines.text: <humming off-tune>

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37284
lines.text: I'm sorry, can you please just... Stop?

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63295
lines.text: Oh, yeah, sorry. Sure.

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63294
lines.text: <humming>

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37281
lines.text: <big sigh>

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37315
lines.text: Give me a supply status rundown.

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63326
lines.text: We're still waiting on... We're still waiting on most requested shipments from the Oldest House. Low on analgesics, black rock injector fluid, coffee.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37313
lines.text: So everything, basically.

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63324
lines.text: Yup.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37306
lines.text: Sometimes I think the Bureau is more interested in our patients' test results than our treatment success.

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63317
lines.text: Yeah, maybe...

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37304
lines.text: I was really hoping for a different answer.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37276
lines.text: Correct.

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63287
lines.text: Knew it. Thanks.

lines.speaker: FIELDHOSPITALWORKER_63290
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37286
lines.text: That's right. Thank you.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_37289
lines.text: That's fine.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_14344
lines.text: By the way, I examined the twin sisters you had brought in.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_14346
lines.text: There you are. I examined the twin sisters you had brought in.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_14347
lines.text: The first patient, Heidi, is uninjured, but understandably in shock. She insisted Hannah is not her sister. Hannah herself is... not very responsive. It could be a cognitive injury, severe PTSD, or... Something paranatural that I'm too new to even guess at.

options.text: Heard the Pattern is impacting people?
Do you like the FBC so far?
How’d you end up in the tunnels?
Had a chance to study the Mold?
Did you know about FBC before?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_14354
lines.text: Hannah's not Heidi's sister? I mean, they're identical...

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32036
lines.text: Like I said, Heidi was in shock. I ran a few tests to reassure her, but without genetic testing, which I don't have the setup for here, it's impossible to confirm definitively.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_32037
lines.text: I'll go talk to her.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_14359
lines.text: Didn't they tell you? Heidi is missing.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32038
lines.text: It was in my report.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_14361
lines.text: Apparently there's a shortage of Mold PPE, so I can barely even check on my patient. But you can. Maybe you can search the cell. Try to talk to Hannah. Let me know what you can find, okay?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_14366
lines.text: Heidi was in shock and very insistent that Hannah is not her sister. But I'm more concerned about Hannah. She's borderline catatonic.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_21545
lines.text: Oh, Dylan! Have you met Fred yet?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_21544
lines.text: You... know Fred too?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_21543
lines.text: Of course! I've known him since... well, it doesn't matter. Isn't he just great?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_31217
lines.text: I know I haven't worked here long, but as far as I can tell, Fred is single-handedly holding the Bureau together. And making all our lives better. I can't even remember what it was like before I knew him...

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_31216
lines.text: Or when that even was.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31219
lines.text: What exactly makes Fred so great?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_31220
lines.text: Have you ever met someone and just known instantly that they get you? Maybe even more than you get yourself? And that they're absolutely incredible? That's Fred.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_31221
lines.text: Anyway, I'm sure you don't want to listen to me going on about Fred. What's up?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31223
lines.text: Hold on. You don't remember when you first met Fred? It couldn't have been that long ago.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_31224
lines.text: Well, when you really hit it off with someone, it's like you've known them forever, right?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_31225
lines.text: Anyway, I'm sure you didn't come here just to talk about Fred - even though I'd love to. What's up?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31227
lines.text: Uh, right. Sure. Fred's the best.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_32033
lines.text: Did you have any news on those twin sisters I found in the Park?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32034
lines.text: Oh! Yes, I examined them.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32040
lines.text: Heidi's disappearance is the whole reason I called you here.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_32042
lines.text: Did Heidi say anything, before she left?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32043
lines.text: No, not to me and not to any of my staff.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_32045
lines.text: She left without Hannah? She wouldn't go anywhere without her sister before.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32046
lines.text: Heidi was carrying a lot of guilt over what happened. She may be in denial over her sister's condition.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_32048
lines.text: But... how did she even get out?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32049
lines.text: It's quarantine, not prison. And security around here is more concerned with keeping what's outside from getting in.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32051
lines.text: How'd it go with Hannah?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_32055
lines.text: Heidi left a note behind. Said the rescue team found Hannah on the street, not at her home? Is that true?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32056
lines.text: I don't know. Why?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_32054
lines.text: She's not talking, like you said.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32060
lines.text: Dylan. I have an update on the twins. The current working theory is that Hannah may have been a latent, uh, parahuman... paranormal...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_32061
lines.text: Parautilitarian?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32062
lines.text: Yes. Hannah eating the Mold resulted in an unexpected reaction.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32063
lines.text: They think with enough testing and help from Bureau Mold experts, I can tell them why and how. We'll see.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32064
lines.text: As I was saying, the theory is if Hannah was a parautilitarian, even a weak one, her abilities may have interacted with the Mold in unexpected ways.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32066
lines.text: The Bureau's hoping that with the help of some Mold experts, I can figure out how...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_32069
lines.text: Do you think she... created the copies, on purpose somehow? As... substitutes for Heidi?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32068
lines.text: That's... an interesting theory, but we don't know enough to speculate. It could just be a reaction, an evolution of the Mold in a new host. Or... maybe there's more to it. I'm not a medical researcher, but I do know one thing: there's no point in guessing.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_32072
lines.text: If Hannah was a parautilitarian, could Heidi be one too?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32071
lines.text: That's the question everyone's asking. There aren't any signs of that so far. But I'm told there's quite the precedent with you and your sister. Though Hannah's abilities were nowhere near your level, apparently.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_32075
lines.text: Is Heidi here? Will she be brought back to quarantine?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32074
lines.text: They're taking her to a more secure observation space in the Oldest House. She needs to be monitored for Mold.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_32077
lines.text: And after that? If she's okay?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32076
lines.text: Shouldn't you know more about this than I do? She'll be held with all the other surviving civilians, for now. I don't know what happens after that.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_32079
lines.text: Anyway, I just thought you'd want to know.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_32080
lines.text: Yeah, thanks.

lines.text: DR FLOREZ

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33113
lines.text: Excuse me, Dr. Florez?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_33114
lines.text: You here for the body? Oh, it's you. Sorry, I was expecting a morgue transport.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33116
lines.text: A... body?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_33117
lines.text: DR FLOREZ

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33118
lines.text: DYLAN

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_33119
lines.text: DR FLOREZ

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33122
lines.text: You mean... the headless body?

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_33123
lines.text: DR FLOREZ

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_33120
lines.text: Did you see the body?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33121
lines.text: Yeah, I saw it.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_33124
lines.text: The problem is obvious, right? I have a deceased patient with an internal, apparently idiopathic cranial blast injury. I received a medic recommendation -- which I agree with -- to find and quarantine-uh-- Contain anyone with a known exposure until we know more.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_58654
lines.text: DR FLOREZ

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33125
lines.text: I can try.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_33126
lines.text: Good. Keep me updated, will you?

lines.text: DR FLOREZ

lines.text: DR FLOREZ

lines.text: I should get back to work. Keep me updated.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_33148
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: DRFLOREZ_33149

lines.text: Where is it?

lines.text: Are my coupons still good?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58542
lines.text: Hope the real Panopticon is holding up without me... I'll be back soon.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58543
lines.text: Wonder if I'm getting sick... <cough> Can't tell...

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58544
lines.text: <humming>

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58545
lines.text: Hope we find another Altered Item soon... Maybe even an Object of Power.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58546
lines.text: Let's see here... Hm...

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58547
lines.text: I could send my guards to find my car...

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58548
lines.text: Wonder if I could get the Rangers to move my furniture up from my apartment. Don't wanna have to buy new stuff...

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58549
lines.text: I should make Alfred a special meal, after I was gone so long... Maybe-- No... Not good for his cholesterol. Something else...

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58550
lines.text: Hope Alfred's eating enough...

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58551
lines.text: I wonder if it's too cold for the Altered Items... Maybe we need...containment blankets. Just in case.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58552
lines.text: Glad the radio didn't turn out like that milk carton they brought in from Washington state a few years back... I can still hear the crying...

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58554
lines.text: "Frederick Langston, for your heroic deeds during the Manhattan AWE...". I couldn't have done it without my work ethic, my years of experience, and my best friend, Alfred... Oh, no, no, no, no, I'm not camera shy.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58555
lines.text: How is the door stuck again?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58539
lines.text: Do you think he knows?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58538
lines.text: I don't think he knows.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58537
lines.text: You don't think I know what?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58536
lines.text: It's tragic, really.

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58535
lines.text: Absolutely.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58534
lines.text: Hello?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58533
lines.text: I don't think we should tell him.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58532
lines.text: Are you talking about me?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58531
lines.text: <trying to hold back a snicker>

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58530
lines.text: No. Not yet. He's not ready.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58529
lines.text: Ready for what?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58528
lines.text: Hey, if everything went wrong, would you two have to, you know... Jump in front of Hiss to save my life? That's the deal, right? You're supposed to guard me?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58527
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58526
lines.text: Oooh, he really doesn't know.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58525
lines.text: Know what?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58524
lines.text: Poor guy.

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58523
lines.text: Okay, you're stuck where he is. The thing is, you can't... die twice. I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58522
lines.text: What does that even mean?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58521
lines.text: Hey, what time is it?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58520
lines.text: Uh... Hang on.

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58519
lines.text: Leckie, did you feel a shudder in the air?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58518
lines.text: Huh?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58517
lines.text: Do the thing.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58516
lines.text: Did you hear me?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58515
lines.text: Oh, yeah.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58514
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58513
lines.text: Where did you put that paperwork? Did you move it?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58512
lines.text: I think he's trying to communicate.

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58511
lines.text: If someone's here who wants to talk to us, tap on my shoulder now.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58510
lines.text: You can see me. I'm here.

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58509
lines.text: Huh... Nothing.

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58508
lines.text: <trying to cover a snicker>

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58507
lines.text: Did we hear from Hashim yet? He never got back to me about the--

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58506
lines.text: You still don't know? No one else can see or hear you.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58505
lines.text: Then how can you? Huh?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58504
lines.text: We have the "Sight".

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58503
lines.text: That's-- I talk to other people all the time. They talk back to me.

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58502
lines.text: I wonder when his agony will end. Will he ever pass on? Walk towards the light, it's okay...

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58501
lines.text: He must have unfinished business.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58500
lines.text: Just stop! Stop it!

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58499
lines.text: Hey. Padmore. Leckie. You're not really doing anything useful here, right? -- and there's lots of other guards around anyway -- maybe you could take a quick trip down the Sinkhole, pick up some of my furniture, and bring it back?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58498
lines.text: We're not a moving company.

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58497
lines.text: You can't use furniture anymore. You'd just... float right through it.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58496
lines.text: I'm not-- I am NOT A GHOST!

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_59753
lines.text: <trying to cover a snicker>

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58494
lines.text: God...Dammit!

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58493
lines.text: Did you actually move his terminal?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58492
lines.text: No. How? You think I'm that strong?

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58491
lines.text: I dunno.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58559
lines.text: AWE.  Altered World Event. AWE. Amazing, whimsical, existential. AWE. A. W. E.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_60008
lines.text: Awe. Awe-inspiring.  Lonely. But there's no I in AWE. AWE. A. W. E.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58558
lines.text: Terrifying. Mystifying. A. W. E...  Huh.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58557
lines.text: Existential. Uh... Existential. Exponential... Utensil. Dammit.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58556
lines.text: Existential. But focus on a pencil. The world is ending, the ice cream's melting, the web is ripping apart. But the pencil isn't sharp... Focus on the pencil, not the existential... A... W... E...

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_58553
lines.text: It's just, you never know.

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_60019
lines.text: Oh god, it's so cold here all of a sudden. Brrrrhhhh.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_20694
lines.text: So is Fred, er, Fra dangerous?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_20695
lines.text: Dangerous is such an ugly word. He hasn't hurt anyone. That we know of. Not per se.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_20696
lines.text: What does that mean?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_20697
lines.text: Everyone always assumes that just because you don't know much about a Paranatural Entity, that means they must be scary.  Does anyone try to get to know them? To understand? No.

options.text: I am still looking for the subwoofer
Any speakers come through the Bureau?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_20699
lines.text: What exactly is Fred, uh, Fra?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_20700
lines.text: He's a Paranatural Entity. A little difficult to categorize, actually. The Bureau brought him up here all the way from Houston, Texas. He's been with the FBC a long time, longer than me if you can believe it. You know, your sister used to go talk to him every once in awhile. He's a very unique individual. Uh, Entity.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_20707
lines.text: Actually, I agree with you completely.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_20708
lines.text: Oh, right. You're kind of a Paranatural Entity. You're a parautiliarian, after all, just not the good kind like your sister.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_20709
lines.text: Not that you're not a good parautilitarian. I mean, you saved our asses, right?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_20710
lines.text: Just that, I guess you should be the last one to judge.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_20713
lines.text: Wait, sorry, can we go back to the part where you said he's not dangerous "per se"?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_20714
lines.text: He's not going to kill you if that's what you're worried about. I can't guarantee that. There are no guarantees when it comes to the paranatural. But he's never killed anyone before.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_20718
lines.text: Listen, we should get Fra re-contained. It does not look good for the Panopticon Supervisor to lose his supervisees.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_20798
lines.text: Hey, I went to visit Fra in his containment unit, but he's not responding.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_20799
lines.text: Yeah. Weird, right? I noticed that too.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_20803
lines.text: So... You checked on him?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_20804
lines.text: Noooo. Nooo. No. No. No. No. No way. It would not be a good idea to open that door without a full back-up containment unit, which we can't get right now. Fra could escape again. Plus, the door won't open. We tried. But no need to worry, these things happen all the time.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_20814
lines.text: Yeah, maybe you're right.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_20816
lines.text: Fra's not going anywhere if that's what you're worried about. FBC containment units are primo. Indestructible. Like a fortress.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_20818
lines.text: What if he already escaped? What if that's why he won't answer?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_20819
lines.text: Well, if you wanna be cynical, for all we know, the containment unit didn't work and the entire FBC is under Fra's influence again right now. How could we ever be sure?

options.text: Why does Maria take care of him?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_21007
lines.text: The fake Director's Office is up and running for Fred -- uh, Fra. It's looking good, I think.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21008
lines.text: Great! Hope we've got everything he needs in there. He can be very picky.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_21017
lines.text: I talked to Fra again. He wants to be the belly lead of the brightest table. The big table, he said.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21016
lines.text: Let's see here... Frederick Langston's not one to turn down a good puzzle.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21018
lines.text: So he wants to be the lead... The leader. Leader of the biggest, brightest... Uh...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_21024
lines.text: The Oldest--

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21025
lines.text: The brightest...

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31279
lines.text: ...Table!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_21026
lines.text: ...House.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31280
lines.text: That's it! Wait, what? Okay, what you said makes a lot more sense. Fra must want to be the Director of the Oldest Table -- er, House!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_21029
lines.text: The Cafeteria--

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21030
lines.text: The Oldest...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31282
lines.text: ..Kitchen

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21032
lines.text: ...House.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31283
lines.text: That's it! We did it! Wait, what did you say?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31284
lines.text: Same thing you said. The Oldest House.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31285
lines.text: Fra must want to be the Director.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21039
lines.text: Speaking of -- have you noticed people around the Field Office acting a little strange? Everyone seems really impressed with some new team lead. Too impressed. No one should be that enthusiastic about corporate hierarchy.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_21046
lines.text: You think Fra is influencing them somehow?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21048
lines.text: Well, there is something I forgot to tell you...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_21051
lines.text: Fra's the new lead.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31301
lines.text: Is it possible they just really, really like him?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21054
lines.text: No one likes their boss that much. Not behind their back, anyway.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21056
lines.text: Listen, when the FBC first found Fra, he'd... Gotten into people's heads. Brainwashed them or altered their memories. They were convinced they knew him.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31305
lines.text: Maybe he's doing it again.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_21061
lines.text: Then we need to put a stop to it. I'll go back and I'll--

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21062
lines.text: No, no, hold on. Think this through. If the Field Office is under his influence, then he's gonna have an army to back him up. An army of researchers and administrative assistants, sure. But Rangers too. Maybe we could... Negotiate?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_21063
lines.text: Negotiate?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_21066
lines.text: You didn't think to mention this before?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21067
lines.text: Well, this is different, mostly. The Fra Mauro AWE report suggested that individuals who spent significant time in Fra's presence began to feel like they knew him. It said nothing about whether or not they liked him.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21069
lines.text: I guess I was hoping it wouldn't come up. The thing is...

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21072
lines.text: All his new fans aren't just gonna let us lock him up.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_71780
lines.text: Hey, you don't know someone named Fred, do you?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21369
lines.text: What could it mean? Think, Frederick, think. Fra wants to be leader of the brightest... Uh... What?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_21371
lines.text: Let's hope Fra likes his new office, huh?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_30636
lines.text: Dylan! Thank you so much again for getting Alfred out of that hole. I'm sure he appreciates it too. He's around here somewhere, chasing mice I bet. You know how Alfred is. By the way, about Alfred being... What he is -- besides my best friend, I mean -- I'll make sure he stays out of trouble, but let's keep this between us for now.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_30639
lines.text: Are you sure that's a good idea?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_30641
lines.text: Look, I plan to tell the rest of the Bureau. At some point. It's a delicate conversation. And once I get a new place... If I can find a way to make it a sort of... containment area, maybe I can keep him.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_30644
lines.text: What do you think he is exactly?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_30643
lines.text: A cat-adjacent paranatural entity, maybe, or another being somehow possessing a cat's body... Or impersonating a cat. Oooh, a Cat of Power. Huh? That would be cool.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_60144
lines.text: So... You have no idea.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_60145
lines.text: Well, I know how cute he is. And how much he enjoys the sound of a can of premium-quality wet food opening. And how much I love him. That's what really matters now.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_60146
lines.text: Uh-huh...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31229
lines.text: Why does he talk like that? It sounds like gibberish.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31230
lines.text: Fra makes perfect sense -- if you know what he means, that is. Which, we don't. Jesse understood him a little -- used to go chat sometimes. She felt sorry for him, you know? Must get lonely, stuck in a containment cell all those years. Wouldn't want to be that guy, am I right?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31231
lines.text: Oh, right, you... You do know what that's like. Point is, Fra's a Paranatural Entity. Who knows what he's trying to say.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31233
lines.text: So... What should we do?

options.text: Why does he talk like that?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31235
lines.text: Nobody gets it. There's a lot more to Paranatural Entities than just death, destruction, and cognitive collapse-inducing trauma. People should try having a little more empathy, you know?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31237
lines.text: I bet Fra has a lot to say, if anyone would listen. Could listen, and know what he's saying, I mean.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31239
lines.text: It sounds like you like Fra.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31240
lines.text: Does it? Well, you spend all your time around Altered Items, I guess you start to wish they could talk back when you talk to them. He might not make sense, but at least Fra keeps you guessing! Better than talking to most of our coworkers, if you ask me.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31242
lines.text: Any idea why Fra would contact me?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31243
lines.text: I don't know. Maybe he heard about everything you've done for the FBC. Maybe he just decided he liked you. Maybe Jesse told him about you.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31245
lines.text: I don't know. Maybe he heard about everything you've done for the FBC. Maybe he just decided he liked you. Maybe Jesse told him about you.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31247
lines.text: We need to get Fra back into containment. Before something goes wrong.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31249
lines.text: So how do we do that?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31250
lines.text: Put him in a Black Rock lined containment unit, ideally. But I doubt he'll go willingly.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31252
lines.text: You make containing him sound easy.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31253
lines.text: Hey, compared to everything else that's going on, dealing with Fra should be a breeze.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31255
lines.text: First thing's first: Find out what Fra wants. If it helps, I think he calls Jesse "Roosa". Try to ask yes or no questions. If he gets frustrated and repeats something, it's probably important. So memorize it, then come talk to me.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31257
lines.text: You never told me how Fra ended up inside the Oldest House?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31258
lines.text: Did I not mention that? He was a stowaway. Came back on the Apollo 14 when they returned to Earth from their lunar expedition. He was disguised as one of the astronauts. Pretty clever, huh?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31260
lines.text: I bet the folks at NASA didn't expect to pick up a paranatural stowaway like Fra, and on a lunar mission of all things!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31262
lines.text: So Fra's an alien?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31263
lines.text: I mean, that's what a trashy sci-fi movie might call him I guess. Not that I hate trashy sci-fi movies -- they can be okay, when you're in the right mood. But no, not exactly. Fra is extraterrestrial, sure, but that's just a subcategory.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31265
lines.text: Then how did he end up on the moon?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31264
lines.text: That right there is the real question. We have no idea. It's a mystery!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31267
lines.text: Fra's wearing a full body containment suit, head to toe. Do we know what he actually looks like? Underneath?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31268
lines.text: That's what he looks like! A containment suit, apparently. He used to be a space suit. Maybe he's trying to blend in with the FBC crowd now.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31273
lines.text: He is the suit?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31274
lines.text: Well, we don't know what's inside the suit. But he's pretty possessive about it.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31292
lines.text: So Fra wants to be the Director of the FBC. Ha! Gotta hand it to him, he knows how to dream big.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31294
lines.text: What will Fra do if he doesn't get what he wants?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31295
lines.text: Well, he'll probably yell a lot, at least. Talk in that... Condescending tone of his. But after that, I don't know. It's possible he has abilities we don't even know about.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31298
lines.text: Why would Fra want to be the Director?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31297
lines.text: Who knows. Maybe he just wants to fit in. The Director tends to get a lot of respect around here. Not... Not that I'm jealous. Either that, or he's just power-hungry.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31300
lines.text: Speaking of Fra wanting to be the Director, have you noticed people in the Field Office acting a little... Well, weird, with regards to a certain new team lead?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31303
lines.text: Not sure I'm the best authority on normal behavior.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31304
lines.text: Well, I am. And let me tell you: people are not themselves lately.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31307
lines.text: Fra actually has a bit of a history of getting into people's heads. That must be what's happening in the Field Office now.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31309
lines.text: If you take Fra by force, I think it's safe to assume his fan club will try to stop you. I don't want this getting messy. That would not look good on this year's performance review for old Langston here.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31311
lines.text: So...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31312
lines.text: We trap him.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31314
lines.text: What? Like a cat in a carrier? Put some tuna down, lure him in, and then -- Ha! Gotcha! Yeah, that could work! But what's the tuna?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31316
lines.text: What if we try to keep him happy? Give him what he wants? Kind of.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31315
lines.text: What, make him the Director?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31317
lines.text: We make him think he's the Director.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31320
lines.text: We do have mobile containment units here at the Field Office...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31319
lines.text: We could set up one to look like the Director's Office.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31321
lines.text: Sounds like a plan!

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31322
lines.text: This isn't, uh, cruel, is it?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31324
lines.text: Is tricking Fra into walking into a containment unit that's set up to look like the Director's Office a little... Uh, mean?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31326
lines.text: You got another idea?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31327
lines.text: Well...

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31328
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31330
lines.text: You think he'll know the difference?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31331
lines.text: That's a little presumptuous. But, honestly, probably not.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31333
lines.text: If we're gonna do this, it'll have to look authentic. Ish.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31334
lines.text: I'll get a reference from the real Director's Office in the Oldest House. Then I'll come back to set things up.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31335
lines.text: You might want to hurry. Who knows how fast Fra's influence could spread.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31337
lines.text: Are you still feeling okay? Like yourself?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31338
lines.text: Me? Never better. Well, I do have this knee thing. Always acts up in the cold weather. Field Hospital gave me some painkillers, but I got the wrong ones. Sensitive stomach. I should go back, but you know how it is, with everything going on...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31339
lines.text: Good. Just... making sure.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31341
lines.text: Think this will really work?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31342
lines.text: If it doesn't, we won't be upset for long. You gotta admit, everyone under Fra's influence seems pretty cheery. Very cheery. Unnaturally so. Wonder what that's like.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31344
lines.text: I'll go talk to Fra again. See if I can get him to move into the fake office.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31345
lines.text: Fingers crossed!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31348
lines.text: I think Fred's gaining influence. As someone that inspiring should, of course! I mean, I wasn't able to get him into his office yet. I'm... not feeling like myself. But I'm sure it's nothing! Fred will make it better!

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31349
lines.text: A real stand up guy, that Fred. Some people don't get it, though. Like that Zoe de Vera, up there in the Watchtower, all high and mighty. Who does she think she is?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31351
lines.text: Can you believe de Vera doesn't like Fred? What does she even do in that Watchtower all day? Who the hell is she to judge Fred?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31353
lines.text: Maybe she just doesn't understand him yet. She hasn't spent time with him like we have. If I could just explain to her how great Fred is, maybe she'd change her mind.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31354
lines.text: Now there's an idea! Go tell her about him. Spread the word!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31356
lines.text: You know what? This isn't the first time Zoe's had a problem with authority.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31357
lines.text: If she spent time with Fred, I'm sure she'd come around. But she won't even talk to the guy! You should fire her, on behalf of Fred!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31358
lines.text: I'm allowed to do that?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31359
lines.text: You're like, Fra's right hand. But, hey, do it in person.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31360
lines.text: People don't like getting fired via sticky note, er, radio.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31362
lines.text: Do you think he's onto us?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31363
lines.text: Fra doesn't seem like the secretive type.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31365
lines.text: I hope Fra will be happy in there.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31366
lines.text: I think so, maybe. At least for awhile, anyway.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31368
lines.text: That said, you never know with Paranatural Entities. They're unpredictable little fellas. But that's what makes them so lovable, right?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31369
lines.text: If you get the chance, maybe you should check in on Fra occasionally. Talk to him through his unit's intercom. Keep him company.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_31371
lines.text: If we open Fra's containment unit, he could escape again. Anyway, the door's stuck. Won't budge. Which is weird, I'll admit. But not everything weird in this business means disaster, trust me.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_36770
lines.text: Ever heard of an Altered Item that can freeze things around it? I think I stumbled on a camera that works like that...

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48031
lines.text: Man, I would love to get acquainted with it.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48030
lines.text: Oh. You don't have it yet, do you?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_48032
lines.text: I'm trying.

options.text: If he doesn't get what he wants?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36772
lines.text: The Bureau actually ran into an item once that was... Kind of, maybe similar-ish to the camera you're after. I wasn't there personally -- too busy, the Panopticon never sleeps -- but I read the report.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_36778
lines.text: "Kind of maybe"?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36777
lines.text: Well, the camera could be messing with time. An Altered Item once caused an entire house to go backwards in time until it was just an empty lot. The inhabitants 'benjaminbuttoned' right out of existence! Which is pretty darn neat.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_36776
lines.text: Huh.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36775
lines.text: Less so for the inhabitants, of course. You know what I mean. Hopefully your camera's effects aren't time-based, or this could get messy.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48037
lines.text: We won't know until it's brought in.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_36783
lines.text: Any idea on how an Altered Item like the camera might work? It could help me contain it.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36782
lines.text: Well, I can't tell you the paramechanics behind something I've never seen. And I'm not really a physics guy. Altered Items have their effects, my job is to respect, soothe, and contain. Keep them happy...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_36781
lines.text: Happy?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36780
lines.text: Do we really need to answer the scientific "why" for everything?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48038
lines.text: Anyway, I can't say more until it's brought in.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_36784
lines.text: Okay. Thanks for your help.

options.text: So we try to keep him happy

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36814
lines.text: Well if it isn't the man who captured a camera instead of it capturing him.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36833
lines.text: On film, I mean.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36817
lines.text: The camera's gonna make a fantastic addition to our mini collection here at the Field Panopticon.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48045
lines.text: At this rate, we might have to expand.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_36818
lines.text: I'm glad I could help. I'm just sorry it took awhile to get it contained.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36819
lines.text: Don't feel bad. There's a learning curve to these things. And if you hang out around me enough while I work, I'm sure you could pick up a trick or two.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_48050
lines.text: Sure I could.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_36820
lines.text: You know what's weird? It seemed like the Altered Item affected me differently than everyone and everything else... It was only temporary with me.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36821
lines.text: Well, that could be more of a 'you' thing. You are a parautilitarian, after all. Or maybe you just got lucky. Or the Altered Item made an exception just for you. Either way, I'd take it as a compliment. It must mean you've got a lot of promise!

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36824
lines.text: Anyway, great job out there. Really, good work. And don't take this as just talk -- I mean it. Way to go.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36854
lines.text: Man, the SINKKI D50 set... I can't believe we finally have a new lead.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36876
lines.text: Dylan Faden! Thanks for handling the situation with those speakers. And that subwoofer.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_36875
lines.text: You've got your full set now.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36874
lines.text: And they'll be safely contained in the Panopticon, right where they belong. They seem inert now, but, well, fool me once, shame on me, and all that. Well, shame on the guy responsible for not recognizing that subwoofer was legit, which wasn't me, obviously, that was -- well, he's not with us anymore. Rest in peace. But still, my department. I'm embarrassed.  Hey, all's well that ends well, right?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_36873
lines.text: Huh. Gotta figure out whether they can be stored together, or if I have to separate them...

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48010
lines.text: There's a storage space full of them in the Rec Room.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48011
lines.text: There's a storage space full of them, about halfway to your room.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48012
lines.text: There's a storage space full of them, about halfway to your old room.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48025
lines.text: We need to get him re-contained, A-S-A-P. It does not look good for the Panopticon Supervisor to lose his supervisees. I'm up for a modest pay bump this year.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_48027
lines.text: Hey--

lines.speaker: DYLAN_48034
lines.text: And kind of in a hurry.

options.text: She has a problem with authority

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48035
lines.text: To your question - Kind of. Maybe.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_48041
lines.text: Any idea on how I could catch the camera? Every time I'm close, it just... teleports away.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48040
lines.text: Well I haven't come across this exact M.O. before.  Which is all the more reason for me to get the item added to my collection-- I mean, contained in the Panopticon. Not for my enjoyment, obviously. Look... Sometimes Altered Items just need to... get to know you. You know?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_48044
lines.text: I'm not sure I--

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48043
lines.text: Just keep at it. And don't scare it off, okay?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48047
lines.text: I heard that Altered Item was causing you quite a lot of trouble.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48049
lines.text: I can't wait to get a good look at it!

lines.speaker: DYLAN_48052
lines.text: It seems like there are a lot of Altered Items popping up in the city right now...

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48053
lines.text: Not a big surprise, given the scale of this AWE. It might be making more, attracting them, who knows. Lucky us, right?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48054
lines.text: With everything going on, it's almost like you're my protege, or sidekick. You find the items and I contain them. Don't you think?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_48239
lines.text: So the FBC set up a second, miniature Panopticon?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48240
lines.text: Yuuup. Travel-sized.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48241
lines.text: Bite-sized.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_48244
lines.text: What did Darling tell you about me?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48245
lines.text: You were already locked in the Panopticon when I was promoted, and Darling didn't like talking about you. Not that he talked to me anyway. He surrounded himself with sycophants.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_48248
lines.text: What was Jesse like? To work with?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48249
lines.text: We got along pretty well. She really respected my expertise. Even offered me a promotion once, but I turned it down. I'm happy here.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_66639
lines.text: Go too far in leadership and you lose touch with why you started the job in the first place, right?

options.text: Any idea how it might work?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_48253
lines.text: Why do you need a Field Panopticon? Why not just use the one in the Oldest House?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48254
lines.text: Travel inside the Oldest House is a little... difficult due to the Hiss. I've still got a crew working in the real Panopticon -- we wouldn't abandon it, obviously.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_66643
lines.text: But we also can't easily transport things in and out.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48255
lines.text: And two -- wait, did I say one? It's just safer to stabilize and contain an Altered Item we find in the field in the field. Say we had a... coat hanger that starts fires. You wouldn't wanna take that back right away.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_48256
lines.text: So do you... Do you like it out here?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48257
lines.text: I am A-okay with my work station being wherever the Bureau needs it to be, if that's what you're asking. It's actually in my contract, so I really can't complain. ...As long as it doesn't last forever.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48258
lines.text: The cafeteria's worse out here, though. The sandwiches... Ughh, there's no squish, you know what I mean? Think it's old mayo...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_48226
lines.text: Hello...?

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48227
lines.text: Uh, uh, uh. One quick second.

lines.speaker: LANGSTON_48228
lines.text: Dylan! Hey! Welcome to the Field Panopticon.

options.text: Lots of Altered Items in the city...
FBC set up a Field Panopticon?
What did Darling say about me?
Why not use the regular Panopticon?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64252
lines.text: Any help is appreciated.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64250
lines.text: Hey, take whatever you can.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64249
lines.text: Found something?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64248
lines.text: Thanks in advance, Faden.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64247
lines.text: We all appreciate your help.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64372
lines.text: Hey, Faden--got a sec?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64371
lines.text: Hey, have a minute?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64370
lines.text: Faden, can we talk?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64363
lines.text: I heard you're the reason Arish is still with us. Thanks for getting him out of there.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64369
lines.text: Do you have a sec?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64368
lines.text: Nice to see you.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64367
lines.text: Do I know you?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64366
lines.text: No, but they told me about you. My name's Ruboneka, Chief Logistics Officer.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64365
lines.text: Actually, Head of Operations now. Still getting used to the new title.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64364
lines.text: I was promoted... After everything with Arish.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64362
lines.text: He and I used to be friends, back in the day, before I got stuck outside during the lockdown. Listen, I could use your help, if you have the time.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64361
lines.text: Look, I heard you and Arish don't get along. You'll have to forgive me -- I'm just glad to see an old friend still alive. I thought for sure he was gone.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64360
lines.text: I never thought I'd be taking my old friend's job. Then again, this whole AWE wasn't on my bingo card. But I would've preferred to fight it side by side with Arish.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64359
lines.text: Anyway. If you've got the time, I could use your help.

options.text: Why don’t you talk to him?
At least you saved your friend
Said you know who I am?
How was it outside the lockdown?
Aren’t you worried about the Hedron?
A lot of us had hard lives

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64358
lines.text: What do you need help with?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64357
lines.text: Well, essentially... Everything.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64356
lines.text: They replaced Arish already? That seems... fast.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64355
lines.text: Things do move fast around here. Leadership roles can't stay empty in a crisis.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64354
lines.text: Listen...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64353
lines.text: Chief Logistics Officer?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64352
lines.text: After we lost contact with the Oldest House, Operations in NYC fell on my plate. Technically I'm a Ranger, but with more responsibility and no additional pay. The job was going a lot more smoothly before the lockdown fell.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64351
lines.text: Listen...

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64350
lines.text: You see this task board? We're setting them up in every zone we can. There's too much work to go around, and a lot of it's unsafe for anyone who's not a Person of Power like you. I know you've got higher priorities, but if you see anything you can help with, do it. Please.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64312
lines.text: Hey, Faden. You haven't talked to Arish since his suspension, have you? He kicked everyone out of their posts in the Verconn lobby. Won't let anyone back in. I'm... I'm concerned.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64311
lines.text: Yeah... I did actually. He's... not doing great.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64310
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64309
lines.text: No, he's not. Thanks for letting me know.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64308
lines.text: No, I haven't... If he's gonna talk to someone, I doubt it would be me...

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64307
lines.text: Maybe not. Thanks anyway.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64306
lines.text: You're friends, right? Haven't you talked to him?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64305
lines.text: I try. But honestly? I think he's... Ashamed. Look, no pressure, but... Maybe he'd listen to somebody who's... been there. Just a thought.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64304
lines.text: Hey, Dylan. Look, I've got some news: The Bureau promoted me to Head of Operations. I don't mind the upgrade, but it does feel wrong taking Arish's job.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64303
lines.text: They replaced Arish already? That seems... Fast.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64302
lines.text: Things do move fast around here. Leadership roles can't stay empty in a crisis.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64301
lines.text: Uh, congratulations?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64300
lines.text: They're not in order. At least not now. I wasn't exactly angling for a promotion. And it's really the same work I was doing before the lockdown fell, just finally comes with a pay raise. And a lot more existential danger.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64299
lines.text: Point is, if you have any H.O.O. Business, you can bring it to me from now on.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64298
lines.text: Hey, Ruboneka.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64297
lines.text: Faden. You know, I wasn't even meant to be in Manhattan when the AWE hit? I was supposed to be having a day off with my wife and kids... Don't worry, they weren't in the city when the lockdown fell. Anyway, I ended up filling in for a friend on sick leave instead. That's the only reason I'm here.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64296
lines.text: Well... At least you saved your friend, right?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64295
lines.text: Unfortunately, she lived in the city. They think she was asleep when it happened. They couldn't recover the body -- too high up, even if we had a free crane...

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64294
lines.text: She might've had a better chance if I hadn't filled in, funnily enough...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64293
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64292
lines.text: I don't think everything happens for a reason. At least the Bureau has never found scientific evidence of that, but... It would be easier to take if it did.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64291
lines.text: I'm sorry that you're separated from your family.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64290
lines.text: I'm not. I love my family, which is why, if an AWE of this scale was going to happen... I'm glad I'm here, making sure nothing ever gets out.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64289
lines.text: Well, no pressure, but I'm counting on you to get me home in time for Christmas.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64288
lines.text: And who knows, maybe I'll be home for Christmas.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64287
lines.text: Hey, Faden.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64286
lines.text: Hey. Are you okay?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64285
lines.text: Yeah, I will be.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64284
lines.text: I don't... I don't do regret. We make our choices, and we live with them.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64283
lines.text: After what happened to Arish -- can't help but think... If I'd just stopped him from leaving, then maybe... Well...

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64282
lines.text: You don't... "do" regret? Do you have a choice?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64281
lines.text: You can't choose how you feel, but... I think we have a choice in what we focus on, hold onto. I'm gonna try not to hold onto this.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64280
lines.text: It wouldn't have made a difference, if you were there or not.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64279
lines.text: Unfortunately, we'll never know.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64278
lines.text: We should both get back to work. Thanks for talking, man.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64277
lines.text: Yeah, sure... Anytime.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64276
lines.text: Hey, Faden... I wanted to ask -- Arish, you were with him, weren't you? You fought that Resonant together?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64275
lines.text: Yeah, I was with him. He wasn't alone.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64274
lines.text: Good. Good, I'm glad to hear that.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64273
lines.text: I was there. He... He died a hero.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64272
lines.text: I'm just glad he wasn't alone. Thanks.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64271
lines.text: Arish... He was the Resonant.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64270
lines.text: What... That's? That's... Not what... How?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64269
lines.text: I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64268
lines.text: You're serious, aren't you? I... I'm sorry he went through that after everything else. He never caught a break.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64267
lines.text: You said before... You know who I am? And you're... Okay to work with me?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64266
lines.text: Right now, all I see is another person trying to get through this mess, just like the rest of us. So yeah, and yes. We're good.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64265
lines.text: So you were outside, during the lockdown? HQ going dark must have been... A surprise.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64264
lines.text: That's one way to put it. It took awhile to get everything running smoothly without our central leadership. But the FBC is more than just the Oldest House. For anyone stationed in Manhattan, though, most of the time was spent monitoring the Oldest House, looking for any signs of movement, or... life. We really thought everyone was dead.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64263
lines.text: You said you were friends with Arish... Was he--

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64262
lines.text: Always so friendly? No. Whatever happened during the lockdown... It changed him. It might help to know, because he never talks about it -- Arish had a hard life growing up, lost a lot of people close to him. There must be something left of the guy I used to know, beneath all that anger. Maybe he just needs to get back in the ring, blow off some steam.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64254
lines.text: You seem pretty laid back, given that the world could be ending.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64253
lines.text: The world's always ending. Especially in our line of work. It's just a little accelerated right now.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64261
lines.text: The ring?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64260
lines.text: Boxing. Yeah, we used to go once a week. Meet up after work, talk for a while, then punch each other. It was good. Though these days I prefer yoga.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64259
lines.text: He's not the only one who had a hard life...

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64258
lines.text: It's certainly not an excuse. But it's also not a competition.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64257
lines.text: He lost even more, because of me.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64256
lines.text: Yes, he did.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64255
lines.text: Look... Sometimes trauma doesn't let you see the big picture. Arish is just... Not seeing the forest for the trees. He's stuck. But he can get unstuck. Probably.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_71852
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_71853
lines.text: Faden.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_71854
lines.text: Hey, Faden. Need anything?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_71855
lines.text: Hey, I was wondering...

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_71856
lines.text: Can I help you?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_71857
lines.text: I just had a question.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_71858
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_71859
lines.text: Ruboneka?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_71860
lines.text: Yeah?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_71861
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_71862
lines.text: Faden. What's up?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64325
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64324
lines.text: HEAD RANGER

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64331
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64330
lines.text: Hey, have you heard from Arish? No one knows where he is.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64329
lines.text: Uh, no... Sorry.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64328
lines.text: Given the state he's in, he's probably just... Raiding a liquor store. Thanks anyway.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64333
lines.text: Ruboneka, hi.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64332
lines.text: I can't believe you did it, Faden. We are officially out of tasks. That's never happened, even before this AWE. It won't last, but I'll take it. Langston invited me to this, uh... Poetry night thing. I might take the night off and check it out. Thanks again.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64347
lines.text: Hi.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64346
lines.text: Faden, I know you're busy, but if you have any time to spare, I could still use your help with some of these tasks. Otherwise they just won't get done.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64344
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64343
lines.text: Faden, thanks for taking some of those tasks off the Rangers' hands. It's appreciated.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64327
lines.text: Hey, about Arish... Look, the CFD failing hit him hard, I know, but disappearing like this... I'd ask you to prioritize finding him. But...

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64326
lines.text: My Rangers will be on the lookout, at least.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64342
lines.text: Faden. They said you were a Person of Power, but damn. You're making me look good out there. Thanks for taking on all those extra tasks.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64345
lines.text: Hey, glad you found some tasks from our boards out there. We were a little worried the boards might get destroyed by the Hiss, or the Patterning, or... By anything, really. It's good to know they're still standing. Thanks.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64348
lines.text: Hey, keep an eye out for our task boards out there, yeah?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64349
lines.text: Hey, if you've got a minute, check out the tasks on the board. Okay?

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64341
lines.text: Hey, Faden.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64340
lines.text: How's it going?

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64339
lines.text: Hi, Ruboneka.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64338
lines.text: Hey there, Faden.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64337
lines.text: Hi, Faden.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_64336
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64335
lines.text: Hey. Nice to see you.

lines.speaker: HEADRANGER_64334
lines.text: Hey. Good to see you.

options.text: Why don’t you talk to him?
At least you saved your friend
Said you know who I am?
How was it outside the lockdown?
Aren’t you worried about the Hedron?
A lot of us had hard lives

lines.speaker: DYLAN_15063
lines.text: Zoe, did you know there's a memorial for Arish at the Field Office?

lines.speaker: ZOE_15065
lines.text: Yeah. I was sort of putting off telling you. Pope decided to keep what happened to him classified. Officially, Arish died a hero, fighting a Resonant with you. For what it's worth, Dylan, I'm not happy about it either.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_15066
lines.text: I don't think Arish deserves to be remembered for his worst moment. That's not everything he was. And it's not who he really was, either. He didn't choose to become a Resonant, Zoe.

lines.speaker: ZOE_15068
lines.text: Yeah, I agree. In theory. Just not sure how I feel about calling him a hero. But hey, it's not my decision.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_15070
lines.text: Why hide what happened to him? Arish was a victim, not a monster. People would understand.

lines.speaker: ZOE_15071
lines.text: You know better than I do that not everyone is so understanding. Anyways, it's out of my hands.

lines.speaker: DYLAN_31721
lines.text: I don't blame Arish for everything -- he didn't choose to become a Resonant -- but he did make mistakes. There's no hiding from that.

lines.speaker: ZOE_31723
lines.text: I agree. But the Bureau hides what it wants to hide. It's out of my hands, Dylan. I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERMATHIS_57924
lines.text: Faden.

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERMATHIS_57925
lines.text: Uh... hey Faden.

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERMATHIS_57926
lines.text: ...Faden.

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERMATHIS_57927
lines.text: Faden...

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERJAXTON_57928
lines.text: Lw Cy Ranger Jaxton

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERJAXTON_57929
lines.text: Mmh.

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERJAXTON_57930
lines.text: ...hey.

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERJAXTON_57931
lines.text: Look at that asshole.

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERMATHIS_57932
lines.text: Hey, Faden.

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERMATHIS_57933
lines.text: How you doing, Faden?

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERMATHIS_57934
lines.text: Lw Cy Ranger Mathis

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERJAXTON_57935
lines.text: Dylan.

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERJAXTON_57936
lines.text: Hello, Faden.

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERJAXTON_57937
lines.text: Hey.

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERJAXTON_57938
lines.text: Hey, Dylan.

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERMATHIS_57939
lines.text: Hey, Faden!

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERMATHIS_57940
lines.text: Looking good, Dylan!

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERMATHIS_57941
lines.text: Yo, Dylan!

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERMATHIS_57942
lines.text: Lw Cy Ranger Mathis

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERJAXTON_57943
lines.text: Heeey! Dylan!

lines.speaker: LWCYRANGERJAXTON_57944
lines.text: Getting shit done, Dylan?

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_57981
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Dewitt

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERBORIS_57982
lines.text: I hate to say it, but we may have lucked out.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_57983
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Dewitt

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_57984
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Levi

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_57985
lines.text: I feel shitty about it too.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERBORIS_57986
lines.text: You guys think Arish is okay? After what he went through...

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_57987
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Levi

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_57988
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Levi

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_57989
lines.text: Fuck off.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERBORIS_57990
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Boris

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_57991
lines.text: This CFD thing... I mean, fuck. I thought Arish had it under control. I thought...

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_57992
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Levi

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_57993
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Dewitt

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_57994
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Levi

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_57995
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Dewitt

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_57996
lines.text: Boris is still missing.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_57997
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Levi

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_57998
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Dewitt

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_57999
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58000
lines.text: Maybe he made it.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58001
lines.text: I sure hope so.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58004
lines.text: And that... thing in the sky. And now Boris.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58005
lines.text: You... heard something?

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58006
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Dewitt

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58007
lines.text: Ah, man...

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58008
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Dewitt

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58009
lines.text: Hey, you doing okay?

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58010
lines.text: Fine.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58011
lines.text: Saw one of our guys just... walking in circles. Just kept walking. And walking...

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58012
lines.text: Shit.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58013
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Dewitt

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58014
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Dewitt

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58015
lines.text: I dunno, man. He had a lot of demons.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58016
lines.text: Yeah...

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58017
lines.text: He always did right by us. But the Hiss, the lockdown... it really wore him thin.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58018
lines.text: Made him into a damn tough sonuvabitch, too.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58019
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58020
lines.text: Mmh.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERDEWITT_58021
lines.text: Hell of a guy.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERLEVI_58022
lines.text: Hell of a guy.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERSPRINGBURN_58263
lines.text: Hey, any news from Arish?

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERBERNIER_58264
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Bernier

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERSPRINGBURN_58265
lines.text: I knew that mission was a bad idea.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERBERNIER_58266
lines.text: It was obviously a bad idea. But he insisted. He wanted to go.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERSPRINGBURN_58267
lines.text: We made it through seven years of hell... and now we lose him?

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERBERNIER_58268
lines.text: I have to say, Dylan Faden is not the guy I expected to save Arish.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERSPRINGBURN_58269
lines.text: No shit. Wild.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERBERNIER_58270
lines.text: All that Hiss at the Evac Site, though...

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERSPRINGBURN_58271
lines.text: The Hiss and Faden do tend to pop up together, huh?

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERSPRINGBURN_58273
lines.text: That weapon Arish is having them build, the CFD? Thoughts?

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERBERNIER_58274
lines.text: Well... I admit that weaponizing a Resonant corpse is pretty out there. But... kind of awesome too.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERSPRINGBURN_58275
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Springburn

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERBERNIER_58276
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Bernier

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERSPRINGBURN_58277
lines.text: Jesus, what a mess.

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERBERNIER_58278
lines.text: Well, it kind of worked, right? I mean, maybe--

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERSPRINGBURN_58279
lines.text: Lw Fot Ranger Springburn

lines.speaker: LWFOTRANGERBERNIER_58280

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTTARA_57824

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMO_57825

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTTARA_57826
lines.text: Depends on how you look at it.

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMELANIE_57827
lines.text: Lw Cy Containment Melanie

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTTARA_57828
lines.text: But in terms of taxpayer money in salaries and benefits, big savings. So...

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMO_57829
lines.text: Fuck you guys.

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTTARA_57830
lines.text: So you guys outside had it pretty easy, right?

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMO_57831
lines.text: Oh, for sure. No real leadership, big blow to our staffing. But hey, at least we had more money to spend.

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMELANIE_57832

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMO_57833

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTTARA_57834

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMELANIE_57835

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMO_57838

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTTARA_57840

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMELANIE_57841

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMO_57842

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTTARA_57843

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMELANIE_57845

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTTARA_57846

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTTARA_57848

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMO_57849

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMELANIE_57850

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTTARA_57852

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMELANIE_57853

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTTARA_57854
lines.text: Shut up. I need to know.

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMO_57855
lines.text: Which ones?

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTTARA_57856
lines.text: Any of them. Answer the question.

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMO_57857
lines.text: Which seasons again?

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTTARA_57858
lines.text: The past seven seasons. All of them. Answer the question.

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMO_57859
lines.text: They... got drunk and talked shit, I guess?

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTTARA_57860
lines.text: Hell yeah.

lines.speaker: LWCYCONTAINMENTMELANIE_57861
lines.text: Jesus Christ.

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTKAKO_57862
lines.text: Lw Cy Scientist Kako

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTABED_57863
lines.text: Lw Cy Scientist Abed

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTKAKO_57864
lines.text: This is not an issue. You just waltz up to Langston, explain your problem, and ask him to bring out a love potion from containment.

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTABED_57865
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTKAKO_57866
lines.text: Lw Cy Scientist Kako

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTABED_57867
lines.text: Fuck you.

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTKAKO_57868

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTABED_57869
lines.text: I... okay.

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTKAKO_57870

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTABED_57871
lines.text: Uh...

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTKAKO_57872
lines.text: Lw Cy Scientist Kako

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTABED_57873

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTABED_57875

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTKAKO_57876

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTABED_57877

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTKAKO_57878

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTABED_57879

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTABED_57880

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTKAKO_57881

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTABED_57882

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTKAKO_57883

lines.text: <enormously powerful snore>

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTKAKO_57885
lines.text: Oh, shit!

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTABED_57886
lines.text: Holy crap!

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTKAKO_57887
lines.text: You had me thinking he was dead!

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTABED_57888
lines.text: Just dead to the world!

lines.speaker: LWCYSCIENTISTKAKO_57889
lines.text: Goddamn, man. Really glad he's not dead though.

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58458

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58457

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58456

lines.text: Of course!

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERPADMORE_58453

lines.speaker: LWFPRANGERLECKIE_58450
